note: The owner's record of what changed and where to see it. Every pull request that changes what a learner or the owner sees adds one entry at the top: the date, what changed in plain words, and links to the exact place to look. Shown at /owner/#changes.

entries.title: Lessons: method on screen, Example and Scribble as buttons, question pinned
entries.what: Every child's lesson screen now shows only the method text at first. Two separate buttons stay at the bottom of the lesson: Example (the guess and the worked steps) and Scribble (the rough-work pad). Each one that is on turns blue with a tick, and both can be open together. When the example is open, its question (and its own picture, if it has one) stays pinned at the top while the steps scroll under it; 'Make smaller' shrinks it to one line. A screen with no method text opens on its example.

links.label: Solve pairs of linear equations: the new lesson screen

entries.title: Sorting buttons: tap them into glass jars
entries.what: Class 1 sorting is now the approved button design instead of sentences. Red and blue, big and small sewing buttons lie on a wooden table. The child taps Start; a finger shows one big button going into the jar ('one'), then 'Now you'. Each right tap flies a button into the jar and says the count; a wrong one shakes ('No. That one is small.'). Then 'red AND big' is sorted twice: all the red ones into jar 1, then the big ones out of those into jar 2 ('two buttons are red and big.'), with Again (under the jars, never over a button). Everything is spoken, lines never cut each other off, quick taps all count, and what to do is said again after 7 seconds of nothing. A sorting question's 'Break it down' in the lesson now shows the same sort with that question's own buttons, and 'there are 1' now reads 'there is 1'. Questions read aloud no longer end in a stray 'what' ("which are big what"). The 'Now you try' after it is now two more sorts with other buttons (one thing, then two), spoken, with no words to read; a sort with nothing refused counts as right the first time. 'Break it down' (the sort, and the lift) now scrolls the picture into view and starts it at once, so it is heard straight away; a reminder is cut short when the child taps.

links.label: Sorting by colour and size: Start here, Sort the buttons

entries.title: Absolute value: a live number line instead of a still picture
entries.what: In the polygon-area skill (Class 10–11), the Start here idea on the | | bars now has a number line the learner slides. A bar from 0 to the point shows its distance from 0 and reads |−4| = 4. The lift story and the 'removes a minus sign' shortcut are gone; the text now says plainly why the area formula needs the bars.

links.label: Polygon areas: Start here, The bars mean distance from 0

entries.title: The lift ride: Chintu in a building, a lift panel with big buttons
entries.what: The lift is now the approved design. A building cut open: floors above in sky blue, floor 0 is the gold shop, the car park (minus floors) below, only the floors the question needs. Chintu rides in the lift; the child taps Start and presses the big green up or orange down button once for every floor. Each press closes the doors, moves one floor, opens them with a ding and says the floor ('minus one'; 0 is 'zero. The shop.'). A finger shows the first press, then 'Now you.' The wrong button shakes: 'Down, not up.' Quick taps all count. After each move the sum so far shows and is said (3 − 5 = −2), and at the end the whole sum (3 − 5 + 4 = 2), with Again. Lines are no longer said on top of each other. Money and temperature keep the counter.

links.label: Class 1 adding: Start here, Ride the lift

entries.title: Count with me: a counting game for ages 3–6
entries.what: A new 'Count with me' tile on the home screen opens a self-contained counting game: 10 illustrated pages (floor tiles, meadow sheep, pond, garden, mango tree, sea, night sky, hen house, market, road), counting up to 3 on page 1 and up to 10 on page 10. Each page has five rounds: count every one, find only one kind, compare which group has more, make a number, and a quick look at up to 5. Numbers are spoken (English or Tamil), difficulty adapts to the child, a hint glows after 7 seconds, and a grown-ups panel on its first screen shows progress on this phone.

entries.title: Mango boxes: count, then put together on a ten-spot board
entries.what: Class 1 adding now opens with the approved mango picture. The child taps each mango in the first box, then the second (every number is said aloud), a finger shows one mango going onto a wooden board of ten spots, and the child moves the rest by tapping or dragging, the count going on: 1, 2, 3, +, 4, 5. It ends with '3 + 2 = 5', said as 'three plus two makes five.' A tap on the wrong box shakes it: 'First this box.' The lift for 3 + 2 follows as before.

links.label: Class 1 adding: Start here, Plus and equals

entries.title: The counter and the lift for young children
entries.what: On a Class 1–5 adding or taking-away question, 'Break it down' (above 'Work it with me') opens a lift. The child drops +/− tiles (₹ coins for money) and the counter clicks through every number, pausing at 0. Change is counted up from the price. The instruction is read aloud after the first tap. Class 1–3 see no written reasons, and each 'Work it with me' step now states its numbers.

entries.what: Each worked step in a lesson has a Why? button; Break it down opens them all. 1,110 of 1,119 question types have reasons. Each tap is recorded.
